Believing I couldn't keep changing the mental health practitioner every time when I had issues, I summoned the courage to tell a specific mental health professional that her words and actions had hurt me, attempting to build trust, but it was futile. I did speak to the manager. When asked whether I wished to make a formal complaint, I declined, concerned that my complaint might adversely affect their career. I had assumed it would be fine as long as my experience with other doctors was positive. However, it has since had a significant psychological impact on me. It has also affected my ability to resolve matters concerning my own medical condition. This is the first time I have written about this in a review. I am not good at causing trouble or making complaints. I regret that I should have addressed it frankly when it happened. I intend to take this as an opportunity to deal with matters seriously. Dr. Kamara demonstrated exceptional listening skills, creating an atmosphere where I felt comfortable discussing my concerns without fear of judgment. He clarified that there are no trivial questions in his practice, a quality I greatly admire. His meticulous approach to medicine became evident as he thoughtfully gathered all my symptoms and delved into the details to identify the underlying illness.

On several occasions in the past, other doctors may have sent me home with just paracetamol, dismissing my symptoms as merely the common cold. However, Dr. Kamara took the time to follow thorough procedures, beginning with a blood test that ultimately revealed a vitamin deficiency as the root cause of my discomfort. This underscores the importance of a doctor recognising that, even when symptoms resemble those of cold, flu, or COVID-19, other serious health issues can still be present and require attention.
